lead: America's creative industries have lost 200,000 jobs in four years with no recession to blame, and a blogger writes the field guide for sites that want AI agents as readers.

sections.title: Creative work under the machine
sections.intro: Apricitas counts 200,000 US creative-industry jobs lost in four years - recession-grade losses with no recession - and asks how much of it is AI.

sections.title: Websites learn to talk to agents
sections.intro: A static-blog author ships a full recipe for agent-readable publishing: markdown mirrors, content negotiation, llms.txt and explicit crawler signals.

sections.title: Agents enter the clinic
sections.intro: Baba raises $40M to put AI care teams in front of Medicare and Medicaid patients, with a benchmark for long-horizon patient advocacy in tow.

sections.title: Kimi's crown comes with questions
sections.intro: VentureBeat's assessment finds Kimi K3.1 Pro's agentic benchmarks genuinely historic but its reasoning gains modest, its self-hosting story unfinished, and its launch shadowed by unverified but ugly allegations of an undisclosed paid influencer campaign.

sections.title: Debt secured by GPUs
sections.intro: Bloomberg traces the chip-backed debt boom - on track for $1 trillion - back to Blackstone's 2023 CoreWeave loan.
